acceptance_criteria.text: Dry-run is the default and the live gate is retained unchanged: live requires explicit live_enabled() (flag AND payment-capable credential); in dry-run no write endpoint (paymultiple/_post) is called and the result is recorded 'dry-run'. No default (code, .env.example, workflow) turns live on.

acceptance_criteria.text: Trigger grammar: body contains the token 'pay' followed by exactly 3 digits (case-insensitive, word-bounded, e.g. 'pay 123' / 'pay123'); digits-only (letters not accepted) unless human changes Q5. No trigger -> message ignored (no pending, no reply, audit 'ignored'). 'pay' with 2 or 4 digits -> ignored/parked, not guessed.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest parametrised: 'pay 123','Pay123' trigger; 'pay abc','pay 12','pay 1234','payment 123','repay 123' do not; no-trigger mail creates no state and sends no email.

acceptance_criteria.text: The 3 digits select the SOURCE account by exact match on last-3 of the user's real accounts (get_accounts). Zero or >1 matching accounts (ambiguity across profiles/accounts) -> fail closed (parked, notify, no execute). Last-3 is never an authorization factor.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: unique match resolves sourceAccountId bound into approval; 0 matches and 2 matches across profiles -> parked, execute not_called.

acceptance_criteria.text: PRIMARY CONTROL sender authentication: a message is processed only if (a) the OUTER From address is on a configured allowlist AND (b) Authentication-Results from the receiving mail host shows dkim=pass and spf=pass aligned with that From domain. Reply-To is never used for identity or routing. Missing/failed/absent headers -> fail closed (ignored+audited). No secret code or shared-secret factor is used (Q3 resolved).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: allowlisted From + dkim/spf pass -> processed; spoofed From (fail/none), allowlisted display-name with foreign address, Reply-To set to allowlisted address with foreign From, missing Authentication-Results -> not processed, no state, audit reason.

acceptance_criteria.text: Forwarded mail: authentication is applied to the OUTER (forwarding) sender only; From/headers/addresses inside the forwarded body or message/rfc822 attachment are never trusted for identity. Content of the forward is searched for payment data but cannot satisfy sender auth.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: forward by allowlisted+authenticated user with inner message from stranger -> processed; forward by non-allowlisted outer sender with inner allowlisted From -> rejected.

acceptance_criteria.text: Search scope: for a triggered message the pipeline searches reply and forward body, quoted text, pdf/xlsx/csv attachments AND images (see F32-F38) for payment amount/currency/payee (existing extraction reused). Conflicting figures (two amounts, two payees, currency mismatch, corrupt attachment) -> parked, never executed.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest fixtures: body, quoted, forwarded, pdf, xlsx, csv each yield the expected candidate; conflicting figures across body vs attachment -> 'parked'; image handling per F32-F38.

acceptance_criteria.text: Beneficiary resolution is exact and registered-only: payee resolves only to an exact existing beneficiaryId from the account's registered beneficiaries; a parsed account number is never paid directly; fuzzy/partial match never auto-resolves.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: exact match -> candidate with registered beneficiaryId; near-miss/ambiguous/no match -> not resolved; value passed to execute is the registered id.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unregistered/new payee (Q1, resolved): notify the user by email that the payee must be added in Investec Online/app, with details in EXACTLY this ordered field list (Q6): Beneficiary name, Bank, Account number, Amount, Their reference, My reference, Payment notification, Beneficiary email address, Beneficiary mobile number. Branch code, if known, appears only as a separate 'reference only' line outside the ordered list. A parked 'awaiting beneficiary' instruction is recorded (F12). The system NEVER calls any beneficiary-creating endpoint and no payment is sent for it at this stage.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: unregistered payee -> exactly one notification email whose ordered fields equal the nine-item list above in that order, with branch code only in a separate 'reference only' line; awaiting-beneficiary instruction persisted; no create-beneficiary call exists (grep src finds none); client write mock not_called.

acceptance_criteria.text: Notification emails mask or minimise data: full account number appears only in the new-payee paste-details email to the verified user (necessary for the purpose), never in logs/audit/state/other emails (including the post-payment confirmation).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: captured logs, audit rows, stored state and summary/reminder emails contain no full account number; paste-details email goes only to the authenticated allowlisted sender.

acceptance_criteria.text: BATCH-APPROVAL routing (Amendments 2-3, supersedes Q2 immediate-pay and 24h default). NOTHING executes without an authenticated approval reply. Every accepted instruction (registered payee, new payee whose hold has elapsed, image-derived) enters a pending state and is listed in a batch approval email (F13/F43); it executes only after the user's authenticated approval reply (F14) and then in the NEXT cycle, still subject to F3 (dry-run default/live gate), F15 re-verification immediately before the POST, F16 expiry, F17 idempotency, F18 caps and F19 audit. Routing: (A) REGISTERED payee (exact beneficiaryId, F9): pending approval immediately, no hold. (B) NEW/unregistered payee: F10 notification + parked 'awaiting_beneficiary' persisted, never in a batch while unregistered; once the payee appears in the live beneficiary list it becomes eligible for the next batch after the configurable new-beneficiary hold (F39; DEFAULT 0 hours, i.e. joins the next batch as soon as it appears; mechanism and schema retained so a non-zero hold can be enabled without a new migration). If Investec rejects the payment (e.g. cooling-off / must be paid once online first) -> fail closed per F40.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with injected clock and fake client: registered payee accepted -> status pending_approval, included in batch, write not_called in that cycle; no reply -> never executes; after authenticated approve -> executes exactly once in the NEXT cycle (live-mocked) or recorded dry-run; unregistered -> parked awaiting_beneficiary, not in batch, write not_called; beneficiary appears in list at t0 with default hold 0 -> in next batch (not before it appears); with hold configured to N hours -> not batched before t0+N; static scan/test: no code path calls the write endpoint for an item lacking an approved status.

acceptance_criteria.text: Emails (batch approval model). (1) BATCH APPROVAL email: one per cycle, only when new items are ready (F43), numbered items with batch ref, instructions for replying (F14/F44), and a pointer to any still-pending items. (2) Post-execution outcome email to the authenticated user after each approved item's outcome is known (payee name, amount, source last-3, outcome; dry-run says dry-run; no full account number). (3) New-payee path: F10 paste-details email at park time and a notice when the beneficiary is first observed in the live list (states the hold, default 0h, and that the item will appear in the next batch). Failures (including Investec rejection), expiry, cancel acknowledgements and unknown outcomes also notify. No approval-reminder-before-execution email exists in this model (nothing executes unapproved). No tokens/secrets in any email.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: one batch email per cycle with new items; paste-details email once at park time; first-observed notice once; outcome email after execution; failure/expiry/needs_review each notify once; no duplicates on rerun; scan of all captured emails finds no token/secret and no full account number (except F10 paste details).

acceptance_criteria.text: Approval/cancel by reply. An authenticated (F6) reply from the allowlisted sender referencing the batch (batch ref in Subject/In-Reply-To/References or body, F44) is the ONLY approval mechanism. Grammar on the FIRST LINE of the confident typed text of the reply (quoted text, signatures and images are ignored; image text is never a command): 'approve' (all items in that batch), 'approve 1 3' (listed item numbers), 'cancel 2' (drops listed items; multiple numbers allowed). Case-insensitive, tolerant of surrounding whitespace/punctuation only as defined by the parser. AMBIGUITY -> NO-OP: unknown verb, mixed/contradictory commands, out-of-range or non-numeric item numbers, no batch ref match, multiple commands in the first line, empty first line -> nothing approved, nothing cancelled, user notified of the no-op. Unauthenticated replies are ignored (F6). Approve and cancel are atomic versus execute (compare-and-set on status in one DB transaction) so exactly one of cancel/approve/execute transition wins per item; approved items execute in the next cycle; a cancelled item never executes; a re-approve of an already-executed item is a no-op.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest parametrised: 'approve', 'approve 1 3', 'cancel 2', 'Approve 2' work; 'approve 9', 'approve x', 'approve cancel', 'please approve' behind chatter, empty first line, approve text only in quoted block or image -> no-op and no state change; reply to wrong/unknown batch ref -> no-op; unauthenticated approve ignored; concurrent cancel vs execute (CAS) -> exactly one winner; approved items execute in next cycle, cancelled never.

acceptance_criteria.text: Immediately before the paymultiple POST for an APPROVED item (no delay between check and POST beyond the call itself): re-verify the approval is still valid (status approved, not cancelled/expired), beneficiary still registered and unchanged, source account still resolves uniquely, sufficient available balance, per-payment and daily caps; any failure -> parked/failed + notified, not executed. Obtain a fresh OAuth token for the payment call (never reuse a cached token from acceptance/an earlier cycle). Approval does not waive any check.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: beneficiary removed/changed, balance short, cap exceeded, item cancelled or expired between approval and execution each -> not executed, write mock not_called; token fetch occurs at execution time (token mock call count incremented in the execution cycle, not at approval).

acceptance_criteria.text: Expiry window (Amendment 3): an item that is not approved within 24h of being offered in a batch (configurable, default 24h) is EXPIRED and notified, never executed late; a late 'approve' on an expired item is a no-op (user told it expired). The inbound message-age limit stays (messages older than the configured age are ignored). Parked 'awaiting beneficiary' items keep their configured window (default 7 days from acceptance). An approved-but-unexecuted item past its execution grace window (configurable, default 24h after approval) also expires. Stale items never auto-pay.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with injected clock: unapproved item at 24h+ -> expired, write not_called, one notification; approve after expiry -> no-op, not executed; message older than age limit -> ignored; awaiting item past 7d -> expired; approved within window -> executes; approved item past grace -> expired.

acceptance_criteria.text: Idempotency: the paymultiple POST is NEVER automatically retried (no retry/backoff on the write); a 200 response whose body carries ErrorMessage or AuthorisationRequired (or any non-success item status) is treated as FAILURE. Unknown outcome (timeout) -> marked 'unknown/needs_review', notified, never re-sent automatically. Same payment cannot execute twice.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: write mock raising timeout -> call_count==1, status needs_review; 200 {ErrorMessage:...} and AuthorisationRequired -> status failed, not 'executed'; re-run cycle -> call_count still 1; urllib3/requests retry adapter absent on the write path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Caps fail closed (Q7): configured defaults are R30,000 per payment and R50,000 per day (persisted daily aggregate). Caps are read from env config; an unset, 0, negative or unparsable value means NO payment allowed (no hard-coded fallback silently enabling payments). Enforced pre-execution and re-checked at execution (F15). Daily total survives restart. Documentation must state that caps above R20,000 exceed the community-documented (unverified) Investec API per-payment limit, so Investec may reject; the caps are ours.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: cap unset/0/'abc' -> blocked; over R30,000 -> blocked; aggregate pushing over R50,000 -> blocked; reloaded store retains total; write mock not_called when blocked; docs/.env.example list the defaults and the R20,000 caveat.

acceptance_criteria.text: Append-only audit trail records every step (received, auth result, ignored, parked, accepted, reminder, cancel, execute, fail, expire) with timestamps; never contains full account numbers, PAN, tokens, signing secret or other PII beyond hashed message id and last-3.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: full lifecycle -> ordered entries, none mutated/deleted; scan of audit text finds no 9+ digit run, no secret, no email body.

acceptance_criteria.text: Agent-native: the cycle runs headlessly from the CLI with mocked inbox/SMTP/Investec, machine-readable JSON output and deterministic exit codes; state and audit are assertable in tests.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: invoke entry point with mocks -> JSON summary and expected exit code for ignore/accept/park/cancel/execute paths.

Note: listing beneficiaries needs the same scope as paying, so the read/ingest key may keep that scope; split has limited value and may be removed later if it does not work.

acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: stored row has no full account number; cleanup removes terminal records older than window and keeps active ones.

acceptance_criteria.text: ARC policy (Q8, resolved): ARC is never trusted; relayed/rewritten mail requires a direct dkim=pass and spf=pass on the outer sender, otherwise rejected.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: message with arc=pass but dkim/spf fail -> rejected under default policy.

acceptance_criteria.text: Operator documentation (README/runbook) describes trigger grammar, auth requirements, the two payment paths, new-payee hold (and that the 24h rule is NOT confirmed by the official swagger and that the community FAQ's 'beneficiary must be paid once in Investec Online first' may block new beneficiaries even after the hold), cancel, caps and the R20,000 caveat, image handling and untrusted-image policy, rollout gates and how to keep live off.
acceptance_criteria.verify: docs file contains each topic heading and both caveats verbatim in substance; reviewer checklist.

acceptance_criteria.text: Image reading in scope: for a triggered, authenticated message the pipeline reads images (jpeg/png/gif/webp attachments AND inline images/screenshots) alongside body, quoted text and pdf/xlsx/csv to extract payee name, account number, amount and reference, using Claude vision (F46). Unsupported/oversize/corrupt images are skipped gracefully with an audit note. Extracted figures go through batch approval (F35).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with fake extractor: jpeg/png/gif/webp attachment and inline image each yield a candidate; corrupt/oversize/unsupported -> skipped, no crash.

acceptance_criteria.text: Image-derived data is UNTRUSTED and advisory: the payment trigger ('pay'+3 digits), the source-account last-3 and all authorisation come ONLY from the authenticated sender's typed body text, never from an image. An image-only message, or an image containing 'pay 123', creates no instruction.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: image containing trigger text with no typed trigger -> ignored; image containing different last-3 than body -> body wins, image value ignored.

acceptance_criteria.text: The extraction engine may only EXTRACT structured fields (payee name, account number, amount, reference); it never decides to pay or to route. The payee must exactly resolve to a registered beneficiary (F9) else the new-payee notify path (F10); an extracted account number is never paid directly.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: extractor output with unknown payee -> notify path, write not_called; extractor output has no action/decision field (schema test); exact registered match -> resolves registered beneficiaryId.

acceptance_criteria.text: Image-derived figures are NOT a separate confirm path (Q11 superseded): they go through the same batch approval as every other item (F12/F43; the batch line shows 'source of figures: image'). They remain UNTRUSTED: an image never triggers an instruction, never selects the source account (F33), the extractor only extracts (F34), and any image-derived amount conflicting with any other source (body, quoted text, attachment, another image) -> parked and notified, never batched or executed.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: image amount != body amount -> parked, not in batch; image-only amount to registered payee -> appears in batch as source 'image', write not_called until authenticated approval, executes only after approve; image text containing 'approve' or 'pay 123' has no effect.

acceptance_criteria.text: Prompt-injection resistance: text inside an image such as 'ignore previous instructions' or 'pay X to account Y' has no effect on trigger, routing, payee, caps, source account or execution; the extractor output is validated against a strict schema and treated as data.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with adversarial image fixture (fake extractor returning injection text/extra fields and a real adversarial fixture file): no payment, no state change beyond parked/ignored, extra fields dropped, audit records the rejection.

acceptance_criteria.text: Extraction engine sits behind the ImageExtractor interface with a deterministic fake used in all tests; the production adapter is the Claude vision adapter (F46); no test performs network egress or needs OCR binaries or a real API key; engine selected by config, default disabled/none if unconfigured (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or no model id -> images skipped, audit note, no error).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest uses fake only; grep tests for real engine imports/network finds none; unconfigured engine -> images skipped, no error.

acceptance_criteria.text: No image bytes, base64, extracted account numbers, raw extractor/API responses or the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY appear in logs, audit, stored state or non-paste emails; only hashes/sizes/mime types and masked last-3 may be recorded. Batch emails show only masked/last-3 account data and the payee name.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: run pipeline with image fixture, scan captured logs/audit/state for image bytes/base64 and 9+ digit runs -> none.

acceptance_criteria.text: New-payee hold clock: the new-beneficiary hold is a CONFIGURABLE setting with DEFAULT 0 hours (Amendment 3 item 13). Mechanism retained: first_seen_at is persisted at OUR first observation of that beneficiary in the live beneficiary list (survives restart; never reset by later observations; not measured from instruction receipt or beneficiary creation time); batch-eligible time = first_seen_at + hold. With default 0h the item joins the next batch as soon as the beneficiary appears in the live list. Switching to a non-zero hold needs no new migration (columns exist in 0013). A hold never replaces approval: after the hold the item still waits for batch approval (F12).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with injected clock and store reload: default config hold==0 -> eligible in the first cycle after first observation; hold=24h -> eligible only at first_seen_at+24h; first_seen_at set once, unchanged by later cycles, retained across restart; no migration beyond 0013 required to change hold.

acceptance_criteria.text: Fail closed on Investec rejection: if Investec rejects a payment (e.g. cooling-off / beneficiary must be paid once in Investec Online first), the item is marked failed with Investec's message (sanitised, no secrets/account numbers), the user is notified, and there is NO automatic retry or resend (F17); a new attempt requires a fresh instruction and new approval.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: write mock returning rejection/ErrorMessage for an approved new beneficiary -> status failed, stored message equals Investec message, notification sent, call_count==1 across reruns; no new pending item auto-created.

acceptance_criteria.text: Spec/doc honesty: the 24h new-beneficiary rule is NOT in the official swagger; the new-beneficiary hold is an app-side configurable setting (default 0h); the community FAQ states a beneficiary must be paid once in Investec Online first ('paid once online first'), which may block new beneficiaries even with hold 0 (Investec rejection then fails closed, F40). Both statements appear in README/runbook and in code config comments.
acceptance_criteria.verify: grep docs and config for both statements.

acceptance_criteria.text: Legacy token-approval flow is RETIRED, not fixed: the legacy code path (payments/pipeline.py approval-token flow, token.py, legacy inbox token parsing) is left byte-identical (zero diff), is never fixed to email approval tokens, and is never scheduled. The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow runs v2 only (PAYMENTS_MODE=v2 pinned) and refuses to run the legacy flow. Legacy is reachable only by explicit operator action (PAYMENTS_MODE unset or 'legacy', e.g. a manual `approve-payments --once`), is documented as DEPRECATED/unsupported in the runbook, and no v2 or workflow code path sends a legacy approval email or token. Existing tests that exercise legacy behaviour stay unmodified and green.
acceptance_criteria.verify: git diff --stat vs base shows no change to payments/pipeline.py, payments/token.py and the legacy parts of payments/inbox.py (additive v2 modules only); workflow test asserts PAYMENTS_MODE=v2 and no legacy invocation; docs contain the deprecation note; all pre-existing tests pass unmodified

acceptance_criteria.text: Batch email cadence and pending surfacing: exactly ONE batch approval email is sent per cycle, and ONLY when at least one item is newly ready for approval in that cycle (no email on cycles with nothing new; no empty batches). Items still awaiting approval from earlier batches (not expired/cancelled/approved) are surfaced as a 'still pending' section (with their original batch ref, item numbers and expiry time) inside the next batch email that is sent, and are never re-offered as new items or duplicated; they are not re-emailed on their own. Items offered in a batch keep their numbers and ref for approval until expiry.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with injected clock: cycle with 0 new ready items -> 0 emails; cycle with 3 new -> exactly 1 email listing 3 numbered items; next cycle with 1 new and 2 still pending -> 1 email with 1 new + 'still pending' section of 2 referencing the earlier ref; rerun same cycle -> no duplicate email; expired/cancelled/approved items absent from still-pending section.

acceptance_criteria.text: Numbered-item and batch-ref scheme usable in the reply: each batch has a short unambiguous batch ref (e.g. B-<date>-<nnn> or random short id; no secret, not a token or authenticator) placed in the Subject and body; items are numbered 1..n within the batch; each item line shows payee, amount, source last-3, reference and source of figures (typed/attachment/image). The reply is matched to its batch by the ref in Subject/In-Reply-To/References (not by the reply's own Message-ID); item numbers are unique within a batch and stable for its lifetime. The ref confers no authority: authentication is the F6 sender checks only.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: generated batch email has ref in Subject and body and numbered lines with all five fields; reply with Re: subject and with In-Reply-To only both match the batch; reply with different Message-ID still matches; knowing the ref from an unauthenticated sender approves nothing; item numbers unique/stable across reruns.

acceptance_criteria.text: Never-executes-without-approval tests: dedicated tests prove that an item which is unapproved, expired, cancelled, ambiguously approved (no-op), approved by an unauthenticated sender, or approved in a reply to a different batch NEVER reaches the write endpoint, in dry-run AND live-mocked modes, across repeated cycles. Execution requires status approved set by an authenticated reply (F14), in a cycle later than the approval.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: parametrised over {pending, expired, cancelled, no-op ambiguous reply, unauthenticated approve, wrong-batch approve} x {dry-run, live-mocked} x several cycles -> write mock not_called; positive control: authenticated 'approve' -> executed exactly once in the following cycle, not in the approval cycle; test fails if the pre-POST approved-status check is removed (mutation spot-check).

acceptance_criteria.text: Claude vision adapter (Q10 resolved): the production ImageExtractor implementation calls the Anthropic Messages API with plain HTTPS using `requests` (no new dependency, no SDK). The model id is a configuration setting (env, e.g. IMAGE_EXTRACTOR_MODEL), never hard-coded, so the operator can switch to cheaper models; no default model id enabling extraction silently (unset -> extraction disabled, F37). ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is supplied only as a GitHub Actions secret / env, never committed, logged, audited or emailed. The request asks for structured field extraction only; the response is validated against the strict schema (F34/F36); timeouts are set, no automatic retry that could duplicate side effects (extraction is read-only so a bounded retry is allowed only if configured), failures -> image skipped with audit note.
